request:
At the highest point of a vertical throw, is acceleration zero because velocity is zero? Make a Standard-depth interactive card that plays over time. Keep the program compact (well under 9,000 characters of source; compute positions in small helper functions and loop over the objects instead of repeating code).

Layout, top to bottom, all inside one frame: (1) "Three moments around the top": a strip of three small snapshots of the tossed ball at -0.10 s, Top 0 s and +0.10 s, up positive, with velocity readouts +0.98 m/s, 0 m/s, -0.98 m/s, the same downward acceleration arrow in each, and the caption "Velocity changes by 0.98 m/s downward" between the pairs. The outer two snapshots put the ball at the same height (0.049 m below the peak) with opposite velocity arrows. (2) Below it, the live animation: two lanes labelled Toss and Drop on one height scale, a lower guide at the toss's launch height and an upper guide through the apex and the centre of the held ball. The tossed ball rises with a velocity arrow (up, shrinking) and a separate, differently styled acceleration arrow (always down, 9.8 m/s2). The second ball sits in a closed gate labelled Held until the apex, then the gate opens and it falls from rest with the same 0 m/s reading; at the apex the tossed ball's velocity arrow becomes a dot labelled 0 m/s. After the top both balls descend together to the lower guide.

Physics: g = 9.8 m/s2 downward, launch speed 3.0 m/s, no air resistance, up positive; compute everything from these equations in the program. The held ball is supported by the gate and must not fall before release.

Mode: Over time, fixed (no sliders). Elapsed time runs 0 to 2u/g (about 0.612 s). Use the manifest timeline: label "Time from the top", displayOffset -u/g (shown time about -0.306 to +0.306 s), playbackRate 0.1, and markers at 0.10 s before the top, the top, and 0.10 s after. Controls: only the native Play/Pause/Replay and the time scrubber.

Put the teaching explanation in manifest.cardDescription (2 to 4 short lines). No explanatory paragraph below the scene or controls.

manifest.title: At the Top of a Throw: Velocity Is Zero, Acceleration Is Not
manifest.summary: Three snapshots around the top read +0.98, 0 and −0.98 m/s with the same downward acceleration arrow. Below, a tossed ball rises to the apex, where a held ball is released from its gate; both then fall in step to the launch height.
assumptions: g = 9.8 m/s² downward, up taken as positive.
The ball is thrown straight up at 3.0 m/s and treated as a point.
The held ball is supported by the gate and does not move until it is released at the top.
Motion starts after the ball leaves the hand and ends back at launch height; playback runs at one tenth of real speed.
manifest.description: Top strip: three panels at −0.10 s, the top and +0.10 s. The outer balls sit 0.049 m below the peak with velocity arrows up (+0.98 m/s) and down (−0.98 m/s). The top ball shows a dot labelled 0 m/s. Every panel has the same downward acceleration arrow, and the captions say velocity changes by 0.98 m/s downward. Below: Toss and Drop lanes on one height scale with launch and apex guides. The tossed ball rises with a shrinking up arrow and a constant down acceleration arrow. At the apex the held ball's gate opens and both balls fall together.
manifest.cardDescription:
At the top, velocity is 0 m/s for an instant, but it is still changing.
Just before the top it is +0.98 m/s, and 0.10 s later it is −0.98 m/s, so gravity still gives 9.8 m/s² downward.
A ball dropped from rest at the apex then falls exactly in step with the tossed ball.
